correctness.rationale: All quantifiers specify finite simple H, δ(H)≥2 and no 3- or 4-cycles. The complement has no isolated vertices. A four-white initial state either has no first move or, after its first move, three remaining H-neighbors of a common center are an immovable white obstruction, ruling out all more-white states by monotonicity. For any three whites, a first move exists exactly when an outside vertex H-sees two of them; minimum degree and absence of C4 then force the other two. Every two-white start succeeds. Counting J=H-distance-two edges gives |E(J)|=∑C(d,2), t(J)=∑C(d,3)+2c6; subtract all 3-white obstructing paths and common-neighborhood triples to obtain (n−3)A−B+2c6. Both independent sequential Python and synchronous C++17 whole-subset verifiers agree across all size-2/3/4 white choices on seven explicitly reconstructed graphs, including irregular examples. Finite tests are not the proof of the unbounded theorem.

value.rationale: An all-orders structural enumerator recovers the precise count of hexagons in an arbitrary minimum-degree-two high-girth graph from the multiplicity of minimum zero-forcing sets in its dense complement. It distinguishes the Desargues and dodecahedral graphs, same order and regular degree, by a nontrivial 40-set difference traced to 20 hexagons. This offers a natural information link between forcing optimization and cycle statistics, unlike a routine scalar special case or arbitrary finite parameter.
